steps.note: Precipitates are removed first by clarifier, microfiltration or filtering; mildly heated milk is preferred.

steps.name: cation exchange
steps.note: At pH 4-9 the positively charged lactoperoxidase and lactoferrin stick to a cation exchange resin (one example cycles skimmed milk of pH 6.8 through it for 3 h).

steps.name: elute LPO
steps.note: Lactoperoxidase comes off first, in 0.3-0.4 M NaCl at pH 4-5.

steps.name: elute secretory
steps.note: The secretory component follows, in 0.4 M NaCl at pH 6.5-7.

steps.name: elute lactoferrin
steps.note: Lactoferrin comes off last, in stronger salt (1 M NaCl, or 0.75 M KCl at pH 7.5).

links.name: US5516675A, Separation of lactoperoxidase, secretory component and lactoferrin from milk or whey with a cation exchange resin

sources.text: A patent on separating lactoperoxidase and lactoferrin from milk or whey with one cation exchange resin; its skimmed milk example is the basis here. The temperature given is the 15 degrees C or less it prefers for large volumes (4 to below 60 degrees C possible).
